text: 中国农历七夕，情人节；一名男子跟一外国籍女子发生sex，付了1500块。
en: On the Chinese lunar Qixi, the lovers’ festival; a man had sex with a foreign woman and paid 1,500 yuan.

text: 被警察查获之后，不服，打起了行政诉讼。
en: After being caught by the police, he refused to accept it and filed an administrative lawsuit.

text: 他在法庭上说了一句连法官都发愣的话：“这不是嫖娼，是‘一夜情’。
en: In court he said something that even left the judge stunned: “This is not prostitution; it is a ‘one-night stand’.”

text: 那天是中国情人节，我是把她当‘情人’看待的，我们是有感情基础的”。
en: That day was the Chinese Valentine’s Day; I regarded her as my ‘lover’, and we had an emotional foundation.”

text: 男子要求撤销行政处罚，打了一审二审，最后高院判了——维持原处罚决定，行政拘留14天。
en: The man sought to have the administrative penalty revoked; he fought it through the first and second instance trials, and finally the High Court ruled — upholding the original penalty decision, with 14 days of administrative detention.

text: 判决翻译成人话：是不是卖淫嫖娼，不看你怎么称呼它，看它的本质——以金钱为媒介的性交易。
en: Put into plain language, the judgement says: whether it counts as prostitution does not depend on what you call it, but on its essence — a sexual transaction mediated by money.

text: 这个案子判完之后，评论区吵翻了；有人说：“你情我愿凭什么管？
en: After this case was decided, the comments section erupted; someone said: “It was mutual and consensual, so on what basis do you interfere?”
‘Personal liberty of choice’......;

text: 还有人竟然拿“国外合法化”当挡箭牌......
en: Some even used ‘overseas legalisation’ as a shield......

text: 同时想起了另一个案子：
en: At the same time, I was reminded of another case:

text: 有个男的跟女友同居三年，分手后把三年里送的礼物列了清单，发微信要求折现返还。
en: A man lived with his girlfriend for three years; after they split, he listed all the gifts he had given her over those three years and sent a WeChat message demanding their cash value back.

text: 女友问他：“我们在一起的时候你说这是爱，分手了你说这是债？
en: The girlfriend asked him: “When we were together you said this was love; after the breakup you say it is a debt?”

text: ”；他没回。
en: ”; he did not reply.

text: 几天后，发来一张律师函的截图——他以“不当得利”为由起诉了。
en: A few days later, a screenshot of a lawyer’s letter arrived — he sued on the grounds of ‘unjust enrichment’.

text: 法院最后驳回了，法官说了一句让人沉默的话：
en: The court ultimately dismissed the case; the judge said something that left people silent:

text: “恋爱期间的赠与，是情感表达，不是交易结算。
en: “Gifts given during a relationship are an expression of feeling, not a transactional settlement.

text: 你不能在爱的时候把它当礼物，不爱的时候把它当欠条”。
en: You cannot treat it as a gift when you are in love, and as an IOU when you are not in love.”

text: 你细品这两个案子的共通之处，当你给ren标上价，就是商品；
en: Taste the common thread between these two cases: when you put a price on ren, it becomes a commodity;

text: 当你给一段关系标上价，就是交易。
en: when you put a price on a relationship, it becomes a transaction.

text: MY为什么违法？
en: Why is MY illegal?

text: 不仅是因为它“有伤风化”，更是因为把ren降格成了“可以购买的商品服务”。
en: Not only because it ‘corrupts public morals’, but more because it reduces ren to a ‘commodity service that can be purchased’.

text: 那些鼓吹合法化的人，最喜欢拿“自由选择”说事（不是蠢就是坏）；
en: Those who advocate legalisation most love to invoke ‘free choice’ (they are either fools or scoundrels);

text: 他们说：“女性有权利处置自己的身体”。
en: They say: “Women have the right to dispose of their own bodies.”

text: 可是你见过有哪个富家女会主动选择去MY的？
en: But have you ever seen a wealthy young woman voluntarily choose to go into MY?

text: 相反，往往是被生活逼到墙角根的人
en: On the contrary, it is usually those driven into a corner by life

text: ——穷、负债、被拐骗、被暴力胁迫......。
en: — poor, in debt, abducted and deceived, coerced by violence......

text: 你还不知道一项调查数据吧？
en: You probably do not know a certain survey figure, do you?

text: 全球被调查的MY女中，超过8成都是被迫的。
en: Of the MY women surveyed worldwide, more than 80 per cent were forced into it.

text: 你管那叫“自由选择”？
en: And you call that ‘free choice’?

text: 那叫“你没得选”，那是走投无路......。
en: That is called ‘having no choice’, that is being at the end of one’s rope......

text: 那你告诉我，如果她没得选，你却把行为合法化，
en: Then tell me, if she had no choice, yet you legalise the act,

text: 到底是在解放她？
en: are you liberating her?

text: 或是在坑害她？
en: Or are you harming her?

text: 还是在保护她？
en: Or protecting her?

text: 因为组织卖淫是剥削，所以在社会主义国家不能合法化。
en: Because organising prostitution is exploitation, it cannot be legalised in a socialist country.

text: 这时候可能会有人问了，那雇佣劳动等等不也是剥削吗？
en: At this point someone might ask: but isn’t waged labour and so on also exploitation?

text: 是啊，按照马克思的观点这确实算剥削，但我认为正确的逻辑是因为某某剥削方式是合法，所以人们应当去反对它，或者至少不应去支持它，而不是用来作为理由，来论证组织卖淫应该合法化。
en: Yes, from Marx’s point of view this does count as exploitation, but I believe the correct logic is that because a certain form of exploitation is legal, people ought to oppose it, or at least not support it, rather than using it as a pretext to argue that organising prostitution should be legalised.

text: 在这个世界上存在着诸多剥削，但我认为一个国家要实现共产主义的话，就理应减少剥削，而不是因为还存在剥削而继续增加新的剥削方式。
en: There exist many forms of exploitation in this world, but I believe that if a country is to realise communism, it ought to reduce exploitation, not keep adding new forms of exploitation simply because exploitation already exists.

text: 否则的话，那不就成了因为雇佣劳动是合法的，所以任何形式的剥削都应该合法？
en: Otherwise, would it not follow that because waged labour is legal, any form of exploitation ought to be legal?

text: 按照这种逻辑，还建设什么社会主义国家呢？
en: By that logic, what is the point of building a socialist country at all?

text: 这好比一个人得了病了，正常人会去医院治疗，而不是表示因为我的病了，所以我则多得些其他病吧。
en: This is like a person falling ill: a normal person goes to hospital for treatment, rather than saying, since I am already ill, I might as well pick up a few other illnesses.

text: 不过我这番话其实也谈不上反驳，因为并不是所有人都认同应该走社会主义国家的道路，因此仅当做发表我的个人看法吧。
en: Still, what I have said is hardly a rebuttal, because not everyone agrees one should follow the path of a socialist country; so treat it merely as the expression of my personal view.

text: 我这里说两句吧，评论区那边九成都是喷我的，我没关系，你们和我观点不一样，聊不来就聊不来嘛。
en: Let me say a few words here: in the comments section, nine out of ten are attacking me. I do not mind; you and I hold different views, and if we cannot talk, then we cannot talk — that is fine.

text: 但某位行动，你私信追着我喷是不是有点过分了，我都说了不想和你聊，你还说个不停，是不是有点过分。
en: But a certain ‘Action’, isn’t it a bit much that you chased me down in private messages to flame me? I already said I did not want to talk to you, yet you kept going on — isn’t that a bit much?

text: 我给了你尊重，我也希望你能给我尊重。
en: I showed you respect, and I hope you can show me respect in return.

text: 说两句废话吧。
en: Let me say a few useless words.

text: 我确实只是个学生，没参与过工作，下面这个模拟也是漏洞百出，法律问题也确实很多，这个我没办法反驳。
en: I really am just a student, with no work experience; the simulation below is also full of holes, and there are indeed many legal problems with it, which I cannot refute.

text: 但是我希望各位想想，如果哪天合法化了，真的懂法律的可就要上了，到时候相关的东西肯定比我的要严密的多。
en: But I hope you will all think: if one day it is legalised, those who truly understand the law will move in, and what they put together will be far more watertight than what I have done.

text: 还有就是总得说一句，欧洲那边确实有很多国家性交易是合法的，但是他们就真的完全规范吗？
en: Also, one thing must be said: in Europe there really are many countries where sex trading is legal, but are they truly fully regulated?

text: 一点问题都没有吗？
en: Not a single problem at all?

text: 开什么玩笑。
en: What a joke.

text: 当然，你如果认为我这里的嘲讽没有道理，那请你把相关报告贴在评论区，让大家看看性工作者真正的样子，也让我心服口服。
en: Of course, if you think my sarcasm here is unfounded, then please post the relevant reports in the comments section, so everyone can see what sex workers truly look like, and so I may be convinced.

text: 而不是只把国家列出来，半点不提及他们这些从业者的生态，那样根本没有说服力。
en: Rather than merely listing the countries, without mentioning at all the realities of these workers’ lives — that has no persuasive power whatsoever.

text: 以下为原答案
en: The following is the original answer.

text: 来来来，我来构建一个瓢虫们想看的合法化世界啊。
en: Come, come, let me construct the legalised world that the ladybugs want to see.

text: A是一个涉世未深的小姑娘，长相清纯可爱。
en: A is an inexperienced young girl, with a pure and lovely appearance.

text: 即将毕业的她和同龄人一样在为工作的问题发愁，这天，校园招聘活动里，有一家公司很看好她。
en: Like her peers, she was worrying about finding a job as graduation approached; one day, at a campus recruitment event, a company took a strong liking to her.

text: 面试官：小姑娘，你的各方面能力都很符合我们的要求，这是我们公司的合同，你看一下如果没有问题的话就签了吧。
en: Interviewer: Young lady, your abilities in every respect meet our requirements; this is our company’s contract, take a look and sign it if there are no problems.

text: A接过了那摞厚达上千页的合同，她原本想仔细看一下，但面试官滔滔不绝的话语总让她难以集中精力。
en: A took the stack of contracts, hundreds of pages thick; she had meant to read it carefully, but the interviewer’s endless stream of words kept her from concentrating.

text: 这份工作很难的，报酬也很多，她实在不想放弃，于是还是签下了自己的名字。
en: The job was very demanding and the pay generous, so she really did not want to give it up, and so she signed her name after all.

text: 但很不幸的一点，在合同的第七百九十八页最底下有一行小字：若工作期间本人未能完全胜任本职工作，则本公司有权对其进行人员调动。
en: But unfortunately, on the very bottom of page seven hundred and ninety-eight of the contract, there was a small-print line: should the employee fail fully to perform her duties during employment, the company reserves the right to reassign her post.

text: 若员工不满足调动申请，可自己申请离职，但在离职期间所产生的一切损失全由该员工补偿。
en: If the employee is dissatisfied with the reassignment, she may resign of her own accord, but all losses incurred during the resignation period shall be compensated entirely by that employee.

text: 刚刚工作的A小姐被安排了很多非常困难，一个人绝对无法完成的任务。
en: Newly employed, Miss A was assigned many extremely difficult tasks that one person could absolutely not complete alone.

text: 她不出所有人的预料，把一切搞得一塌糊涂。
en: As everyone expected, she made a complete mess of everything.

text: 按照合同，公司决定让她去做性服务。
en: According to the contract, the company decided to have her provide sexual services.

text: A小姐当然不愿意，她去申请离职，但过了整整一年申请都没有通过，而这一年里，由于她经常搞砸任务，造成了一笔很大损失，单凭A小姐的家庭，是万万无法偿还的。
en: Miss A was of course unwilling; she applied to resign, but a full year passed and the application was never approved, and during that year, because she kept botching tasks, she caused a large loss that Miss A’s family could never possibly repay.

text: 因为实在还不上这笔债务，A小姐尝试使用法律途径解决，但很遗憾的是，A小姐因为缺乏相关证据，并没能打赢官司。
en: Because she truly could not repay this debt, Miss A tried to resolve it through legal means, but regrettably, lacking relevant evidence, she did not win her case.

text: A小姐也尝试去贷款把债务还清，但因为家庭的资产估价达不到标准，正规平台不愿意贷款给她。
en: Miss A also tried to take out a loan to clear the debt, but because her family’s assets fell short of the threshold, the proper platforms were unwilling to lend to her.

text: 各种网贷高利贷可以借，但利息太高，比公司的债务还要高…
en: Various online loans and usurious lenders would lend, but the interest was too high — higher even than the company’s debt…

text: 无奈，A小姐只能服从安排。
en: With no other choice, Miss A could only comply with the arrangement.

text: 因为债务问题，她不得不努力去接客，甚至在别人休息的时候她也得加班。
en: Because of the debt, she had to work hard to receive clients, even taking overtime when others rested.

text: 有一些客人的口味很奇怪，有的喜欢玩带血的，有的喜欢怀孕的，有的则喜欢排泄物。
en: Some clients had strange tastes — some liked playing with blood, some liked pregnant women, some liked excrement.

text: 他们虽然很变态，但往往出手阔绰…
en: They were perverted, but often spent lavishly…

text: 为了尽快还清债务，A小姐只能去接这些并没有人愿意接待的客人。
en: To repay the debt as quickly as possible, Miss A could only take these clients that no one else would receive.

text: 喜欢见血的，她就生理期去。
en: Those who liked seeing blood, she would serve during her period.

text: 喜欢怀孕的，她就不做措施，等结束之后把孩子打掉…
en: Those who liked pregnancy, she would take no precautions, and have the child aborted afterwards…

text: 这个过程中，没有任何人强迫她，但她不得不干，因为如果自己不能尽快还清债务，家里的一切都要被抵押…
en: Throughout this, no one forced her, yet she had to do it, because if she could not repay the debt quickly, everything at home would be seized as collateral…

text: 很快，在她的努力工作之下，赚到了很多钱，但因为是公司提供了场地和人员还有各类型器材，她得上交一半的工资才能继续待在这里。
en: Soon, through her hard work, she earned a great deal of money, but because the company provided the premises, the staff and various kinds of equipment, she had to hand over half her wages to keep staying there.

text: 又因为她身上背着债务，她又得拿出三成来还债。
en: And because she carried the debt, she had to give up another thirty per cent to repay it.

text: 剩下的两成，勉强能够维持她的生活。
en: The remaining twenty per cent barely sufficed to sustain her living.

text: 但并不能满足她医疗方面的需求。
en: But it could not meet her medical needs.

text: 公司确实会提供免费的医疗服务，但服务范围有限，对她的情况几乎没什么帮助。
en: The company did provide free medical services, but the scope was limited and of almost no help to her condition.

text: 保险也确实有，但保险公司的审核时间总是非常长，而且太过严格。
en: There was insurance, too, but the insurer’s review always took very long and was far too strict.

text: 她也尝试过向公司申请工伤补偿，但公司却以目前的结果是因为她自己作业不规范导致的拒绝赔偿。
en: She also tried to claim work-injury compensation from the company, but the company refused, saying the present outcome was caused by her own non-compliant conduct.

text: 是啊，那些变态的玩法是她自己选的，公司从来没有逼迫过她。
en: Indeed, those perverted practices were her own choice; the company never coerced her.

text: 过了几年，A小姐因为过度劳累已经失去了往日的光彩，她的客人也越来越少了。
en: A few years on, Miss A had lost her former radiance from overwork, and her clients grew fewer.

text: 为了尽快赚钱，她不得不尝试一些更奇怪的玩法。
en: To earn money faster, she had to try some even stranger practices.

text: 也正因如此，她的身体也每况愈下。
en: And precisely for this reason, her health declined steadily.

text: 后来，在一次体检的时候，她发现自己很不幸的感染了某些疾病。
en: Later, during a medical check-up, she unhappily discovered she had contracted certain diseases.

text: 她回想，可能是之前某次没有安全措施导致的。
en: She recalled it might have been from some earlier encounter without protection.

text: 她没有上报自己的情况，因为虽然上报之后自己会得到一笔赔偿金，但也不可能待在这里，而债务又没有全部还完。
en: She did not report her condition, because although reporting would bring her a sum in compensation, she could no longer stay there, and the debt was not yet fully repaid.

text: 她选择了隐瞒。
en: She chose to conceal it.

text: 但纸包不住火，某天，一个顾客来到了公司，咒骂你们这里操作不当让他患上了疾病。
en: But paper cannot wrap fire: one day a customer came to the company, cursing that its improper conduct had given him a disease.

text: 公司对此非常重视，一番调查，发现是A小姐隐瞒了自己的病情。
en: The company took this very seriously; after an investigation, it found that Miss A had concealed her condition.

text: 由于A小姐私自隐瞒了重大问题，她被开除了，同时又必须给公司和顾客进行赔偿。
en: Because Miss A had privately concealed a major problem, she was dismissed, and additionally had to compensate both the company and the customer.

text: 不得已之下，她只能变卖家产，把洞补上。
en: With no alternative, she could only sell off her possessions to plug the hole.

text: 赔偿的问题解决了，但她的债务还没还完，而她此刻已经身无分文了。
en: The compensation issue was settled, but her debt was still not repaid, and she was now penniless.

text: 这些年的工作下来，她唯一学会的就是如何取悦自己的顾客。
en: After these years of work, the only thing she had learned was how to please her clients.

text: 所以她很自然的选择了一个并不那么规范的场所，再度干起了老本行。
en: So she naturally chose a less regulated venue and returned to her old trade.

text: 又过了几年，她老了，也终于把债务还完了。
en: A few more years passed; she grew old and finally cleared the debt.

text: 但这些年的辛苦工作并没有让她攒下什么积蓄，反倒年纪才刚满四十，身体就已经受不了了。
en: But these years of hard work left her with no savings; on the contrary, though only just forty, her body could no longer take it.

text: 人老珠黄，没人愿意在点她，她又一次被开除了。
en: Old and faded, no one was willing to pick her, and she was dismissed yet again.

text: 她的身体已经坏掉了，没办法从事那些体力劳动。
en: Her body was broken and she could no longer do physical labour.

text: 高端一点的劳动她也不会，除了那里，她已经无处可归了…
en: She could not do any higher-end work either; apart from that, she had nowhere left to go…

text: 为了活下去，她只能再度重操旧业，投身于那些最低端的行业里，用早已麻木的身体换取一点吃喝的费用。
en: To survive, she could only return to her old trade once more, throwing herself into the lowest rungs of the industry, exchanging her long-numbed body for a little food and drink.

text: 最后，她的生命结束在了不到五十岁的年龄，像一块无人在意的石头一样被随手丢开，埋进了土里。
en: In the end, her life ended before she was fifty, discarded like an unnoticed stone and buried in the earth.

text: 看到了吗，满意了吗？
en: Do you see it now? Are you satisfied?

text: 或许你们会说我故意夸大，会说我胡编乱造，但请各位仔细想想吧，如今这个时代，这种事情咱们见得还少吗？
en: Perhaps you will say I deliberately exaggerated, that I made it all up, but please think carefully: in this day and age, have we not seen such things often enough?

text: 看看东南亚那些性工作者吧，她们真的生活的很好吗？
en: Look at those sex workers in Southeast Asia — do they truly live well?

text: 还有那些发达国家的从业人员，她们真的生活的很好？
en: And those working in developed countries — do they truly live well?

text: 别自欺欺人了，你们这些想要合法化的家伙们根本不在乎这些人的处境，你们就只是想要光明正大的解决自己的欲望罢了。
en: Stop deceiving yourselves. You who want legalisation do not care at all about these people’s plight; you merely want to satisfy your own desires out in the open.

text: 也别说我危言耸听，上面我模拟的情况甚至都是美化的，全程都在法律规范内发展的，你想想现实吧，这么多规范化的法律，这么严格的执法环境，不还是会产生各种各样的阴暗面吗？
en: And do not say I am alarmist: the scenario I simulated above was even beautified, unfolding entirely within the bounds of the law; think about reality — with so many regulating laws and such a strict enforcement environment, do not all sorts of dark sides still emerge?

text: 真要是哪天合法化了，这些工作者的处境必然会比上面说的凄惨十倍。
en: If one day it really were legalised, these workers’ plight would inevitably be ten times more wretched than what is described above.

text: 也别说什么现在国内黄色产业赚的多，都是自愿的这种屁话。
en: And spare me the nonsense that the domestic sex industry earns so much now, all voluntarily.

text: 现在为什么赚的多啊，不就是因为违法，不就是因为少嘛。
en: Why does it earn so much now? Is it not precisely because it is illegal, precisely because it is scarce?

text: 物以稀为贵，就和毒 品一样，管的严导致现在少，想要尝试就得付出很大代价。
en: Rarity makes things precious, just like drugs: strict control keeps the supply low now, and trying it demands a high price.

text: 真要是合法化了，那瞬间就会泛滥。
en: If it were truly legalised, it would flood the market in an instant.

text: 当初大哥大也是高档用品，结果手机普及之后，这东西直接就变成了普通人也能用的消耗品。
en: The first mobile phones were once a luxury item too, but once mobiles became widespread, this thing turned directly into a consumable that ordinary people could use as well.

text: 而且我希望你们能想想，真要是放开了，你们的家人，你们的朋友，乃至于你们自己，都不再是安全的了，谁知道你的生活会不会出现一个这样难以拒绝的“合同”，谁又能保证你能完美避开所有的问题？
en: And I hope you will think: if it really were opened up, your family, your friends, even yourselves would no longer be safe — who knows whether a ‘contract’ like this, so hard to refuse, might appear in your life, and who can guarantee you will perfectly avoid every problem?

text: 好好想想吧，真的是…
en: Think it over properly — really…

text: （想骂尽管骂，我不会删评论，如果你们的评论看不到了，那就是平台出手了。
en: (Go ahead and curse if you want; I will not delete comments. If your comments disappear, it was the platform that acted.

text: 说一句，答主也不是搞法律的，模拟漏洞百出这点确实没办法反驳。
en: One remark: the answer author is not in the legal profession either, and the fact that the simulation is full of holes is indeed impossible to refute.

text: 但请各位想想，这玩意真要是合法化了，那懂法的人可就要上了，到时候可操作性就原本我这个费拉不堪的例子大多了
en: But please all think: if this thing really were legalised, those who understand the law would move in, and the room for manoeuvre would be far greater than in my feeble and wretched example.

text: 毕竟现实里各种各样的漏洞大家也不是没见过，别真天真的意外合法之后一切都会按法律执行。
en: After all, everyone has seen all sorts of loopholes in reality; do not naively believe that once legalised, everything will be carried out according to the law.
